Q1: Pentachloroethane exhibits multiple known significant hazards, including carcinogenicity, reproductive toxicity, environmental toxicity, oral toxicity, and organ/systemic toxicity (all Tier 1). It also has potential inhalation hazards (Tier 2) and demonstrated low/moderate endocrine disruption hazards (Tier 3). Data on dermal and eye hazards are deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Pentachloroethane is not found on either lists of concern or lists of low hazard. Given some data deficiencies in its hazard profile, this absence may reflect a lack of comprehensive study rather than established safety.
Q3: Pentachloroethane is extensively studied with over 2,100 literature references and a defined molecular structure. While lacking an IRIS assessment, it has undergone meaningful toxicological evaluation, evidenced by an EPA PPRTV and 29 toxicity value records, though a data gap persists for dermal and eye hazards.
